questions.question_text: In the context of computer graphics and digital art generation, what defines a vector graphic image?
options: A) A fixed grid of colored pixels
B) Images created using mathematical paths and coordinate points
C) A scanned photograph of a traditional oil painting
D) Images dependent on camera resolution
questions.answer: B) Images created using mathematical paths and coordinate points

questions.question_text: Which foundational technique is used in relief printmaking to transfer an image onto paper?
options: A) Painting directly on silk screens
B) Engraving lines into metal plates
C) Carving away non-image areas on a linoleum block to leave a raised surface
D) Spraying acrylic paint through a paper cutout
questions.answer: C) Carving away non-image areas on a linoleum block to leave a raised surface

questions.question_text: In typography and poster design, what does the term 'kerning' refer to?
options: A) The vertical spacing between lines of text
B) The alignment of text to the right margin
C) The adjustment of space between individual letter forms
D) The thickness of the font outline
questions.answer: C) The adjustment of space between individual letter forms

questions.question_text: Which structural technique involves building a three-dimensional sculptural form by adding layers of soft clay onto a stiff internal wire framework?
options: A) Subtractive carving
B) Armature modelling
C) Mosaic inlay
D) Papier-mâché casting

questions.question_text: What is the primary aesthetic purpose of utilizing a 'Grid System' when constructing a professional visual poster layout?
options: A) To ensure all colors are complementary
B) To create random, chaotic visual tension
C) To establish a structured, balanced spatial alignment for text and images
D) To limit the number of fonts used
questions.answer: C) To establish a structured, balanced spatial alignment for text and images

sections.section_name: Section B - Theory Short Answer Concepts

questions.question_text: Explain the subtractive method used in three-dimensional clay or stone sculpting. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: The subtractive method involves carving away or removing material from a solid block of stone, wood, or hardened clay to reveal the final three-dimensional sculptural form within.

questions.question_text: Describe the structural function of an 'armature' when modelling a human figure in soft clay. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: An armature acts as an internal structural skeleton, usually made of wire. It supports the weight of the soft, wet clay, preventing the sculptural form from collapsing during the modelling process.

questions.question_text: Define the visual concept of a 'Mosaic' and list the typical raw materials used in its construction. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: A mosaic is an image created by arranging small, colored pieces called tesserae. Traditional raw materials include cut glass, colored ceramic tiles, stones, or shells embedded in plaster or cement.

questions.question_text: Outline the fundamental difference between raster images and vector graphics in digital art formats. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Raster images consist of pixel grids that lose quality when scaled up. Vector graphics use mathematical equations to define paths and shapes, allowing infinite scaling without any loss of resolution or sharpness.

questions.question_text: What are the primary considerations when selecting typography (fonts) for an effective public awareness poster layout? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Typography must be legible from a distance, appropriately sized to establish a visual hierarchy, and visually matched to the poster's emotional tone, ensuring the core message is communicated swiftly and clearly.

sections.section_name: Section C - Practical Composition & Design Layouts

questions.question_text: Develop a practical scoring rubric for evaluating a student's linoleum block relief print layout based on technical carving execution and ink transfer. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Assess the depth and precision of carved negative spaces to prevent ink smudging. Scoring metrics must evaluate the consistency of ink rolling, ensuring uniform pressure during the print transfer phase to yield crisp, solid borders and high-contrast positive image areas on the final paper.

questions.question_text: Outline the step-by-step layout process for constructing a symmetrical, mixed-media theatrical mask using papier-mâché techniques. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: First, construct a symmetrical base mold using clay or a balloon. Next, layer torn paper strips coated with adhesive paste across the mold to build structural rigidity. Finally, after drying, sand the surface smooth, apply a base primer, and integrate mixed materials like feathers or metallic acrylics.

questions.question_text: Define the compositional layout rules for designing a balanced environmental awareness poster using hand-drawn calligraphy and stencil graphics. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The layout requires a strict visual hierarchy. Hand-drawn calligraphy must anchor the upper margin as the primary focal text. Stencil graphics should occupy the central negative space to provide immediate visual context, ensuring the text and graphics share balanced visual weight without overcrowding the composition.

sections.section_name: Section D - Applied Art Portfolios & Digital Synthesis

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the digital curation workflow necessary to compile physical clay sculpture photographs and digital typography into a cohesive Art Integrated Project Portfolio page. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Begin by shooting the physical clay sculptures under uniform lighting. Import these raster images into a digital layout program, applying color-correction and background removal masks. Next, use vector tools to overlay descriptive typography within aligned grid margins. Finally, export the composite page ensuring uniform resolution parameters for a cohesive, professional portfolio presentation.

questions.question_text: Analyze how integrating traditional block printing textures into a modern digital vector illustration software enhances the aesthetic value of an applied art design. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: By scanning raw block print textures, digital artists can inject organic, tactile qualities into sterile computer graphics. This synthesis overlays the imperfections and grain of hand-carved relief printing onto precise vector paths. The workflow bridges traditional craftsmanship with modern digital layouts, resulting in visually rich, multidimensional applied art compositions.
